label: VERIFIED
extraction: Agent orchestration patterns in 2026: five coordination levels from single session to agent teams, with failure modes and selection criteria. Levels: 1) Single agent with good practices (default, most tasks), 2) Subagents for side work that would flood main context (low coordination cost), 3) Headless pipelines for batch work over many items (low, deterministic), 4) Parallel sessions in git worktrees for independent workstreams (medium, manual), 5) Agent teams for parallel exploration with cross-communication (high). Rule: move up a level only when current one demonstrably fails, never because parallelism sounds faster. Token costs scale linearly with agents, coordination failures scale worse than linearly. Level 5 (agent teams) includes cross-model consensus pattern outside single-vendor levels. Strongest conclusion: orchestration is a question of coordination cost rather than framework choice.
